title: Hippos Ooze Red Goo That Isn't Blood or Sweat
subject: hippopotamus

scenes.text: Hippos ooze red liquid from their skin. It isn't blood. It isn't sweat either.
People call it blood sweat. Then scientists analysed it.
It's a mixture of two pigments. One is red. The other is orange.
They soak up ultraviolet light, so the goo works as a natural sunscreen.
And the red one stops the growth of dangerous bacteria, so it works as an antibiotic.
A hippo spends all day in the sun, and it makes its own sunscreen.

description:
Hippos ooze a red liquid from their skin, and it isn't blood or sweat.
It's a mix of two pigments that block ultraviolet light, and the red one slows the growth of bacteria.
Would you want to swap with a hippo?
first_comment: The pigments are called hipposudoric acid and norhipposudoric acid. Which animal would you want to study next?
